To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the speed of the post-crisis recovery of firms depends on pre-crisis characteristics and on the macroeconomic framework.

1) firms with high precrisis leverage have been slower to recover; 2) firms with high asset tangibility have been faster to recover; 3) firms with high short-term debt have been slower to recovers; 4) firms in countries that have experienced a large depreciation of the real exchange rate have been faster to recovers; and 5) in countries with large current account deficits and low levels of international reserves, firms have been slower to recovery.
